member_of.desc: Instead of a profile: the group to put the person in (only with user).

profile.desc: The profile to attach (custom or base, never base.administrator).

access.attach.desc: Attaches a profile to a person or a group, or puts a person in a group. A person (user) or a group (group): one of the two. Nobody changes their own. Refused if it would leave an administrator unable to use access.*. Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps it before and after.

group.desc: A group (not a custom role: those are read-only).

member_of.desc: Instead of a profile: the group.

access.attach.validate.desc: Dry run of access.attach: the same checks (own access, base.administrator, unknown names, already attached, an administrator left without access, limits) on a copy; answers the same errors. Writes nothing and leaves no audit row.

group.desc: A group (not a custom role: those are read-only).

profile.desc: The profile that is the ceiling (it must have an allow rule). Empty: remove the ceiling.

es.text: Cambia lo que pueden hacer las personas, desde su próxima acción. La auditoría guarda cómo era y cómo queda.

access.ceiling.set.desc: Sets or removes the permissions ceiling of a person or a group: whatever they have, they can do nothing the ceiling does not allow. A person (user) or a group (group): one of the two. Needs a confirmation.

group.desc: A group (not a custom role: those are read-only).

profile.desc: The profile that would be the ceiling. Empty: remove the ceiling.

access.ceiling.validate.desc: Dry run of access.ceiling.set: the same checks and errors (needs an allow rule, not a plugin profile, an administrator left without access) on a copy. Writes nothing and leaves no audit row.

args.desc: The arguments of the call (they can escalate it: settings, hardware parameters).

items.desc: Instead of operation: up to 100 requests of the same person, each an object with operation and optionally target, args, mode, mode_now, job_running, machine_on, via. The answer has one entry per request, equal to the single answer.

mode.desc: Mode of the machine: laser, cnc or fff.

mode_now.desc: Use the mode the machine is in now.

operation.desc: An operation name (or <ns>:<name>). Or give items.

target.desc: workshop:<plugin>:<type>/<id> (no wildcard). Left out: the default target of the operation.

access.check.desc: What the access model would answer for a person, an operation, a target and a context: allowed or not, the rule that decided and why each other rule did not match. Changes nothing. With items it answers a list of requests (up to 100) in one call.

group.desc: A group (not a custom role: those are read-only).

member_of.desc: Instead of a profile: the group to take the person out of.

en.text: This changes what people can do, from their next action. The audit keeps what it was and what it is now.

es.text: Cambia lo que pueden hacer las personas, desde su próxima acción. La auditoría guarda cómo era y cómo queda.
es.title: Cambiar el acceso

access.detach.desc: The opposite of access.attach. A person (user) or a group (group): one of the two. Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps it before and after.

group.desc: A group (not a custom role: those are read-only).

member_of.desc: Instead of a profile: the group.

access.detach.validate.desc: Dry run of access.detach: the same checks and errors on a copy. Writes nothing and leaves no audit row.

name.desc: A group or a custom role.

access.groups.list.desc: Lists the groups with their profiles, ceiling and members. The custom roles appear as read-only groups with one profile.

es.text: Se borra el perfil de acceso o el grupo. Solo se puede si nadie lo usa.

access.groups.remove.desc: Deletes a group. Refused while it has people. Needs a confirmation.

members.desc: People in the group. Left out: the members stay; given: it is the exact list (nobody can change their own membership).

name.desc: 1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots or hyphens; not a base role or a custom role.

profiles.desc: Profiles attached to the group (custom or base, never base.administrator). The whole list is replaced.

access.groups.set.desc: Creates a group or replaces its description and profiles (its ceiling stays). Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps it before and after.

remove.desc: true: dry run of access.groups.remove instead.

access.groups.validate.desc: Dry run of access.groups.set (or, with remove, of access.groups.remove): the same checks and errors on a copy (a group with members cannot be removed, nobody changes their own membership, limits). Writes nothing and leaves no audit row.

access.person.get.desc: What a person has: groups, profiles (own and through groups), ceiling, and whether the evaluator governs them.

access.plugins.validate.desc: Reads the permissions.json of every installed plugin, checks it (every operation it calls exists, is classified and is its own or declared shared; the three profiles use only known capabilities; the interface operation ui:<plugin>:open is declared) and registers the valid profiles (plugin.<namespace>.readonly, .operator, .admin) so they can be attached. Changes nothing stored.

access.profile.rollback.desc: Makes an older version of a profile the active one. Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps both.

access.profile.versions.desc: The versions of a profile kept (up to 5), newest first, with who saved each and which one is active.

name.desc: A custom or base profile (not case sensitive).

access.profiles.get.desc: One profile: its document, its active version and who has it attached.

access.profiles.list.desc: Lists the custom profiles (with who has each attached), the base ones and the limits.

en.title: Delete for good

es.text: Se borra el perfil de acceso o el grupo. Solo se puede si nadie lo usa.
es.title: Borrar para siempre

access.profiles.remove.desc: Deletes a custom profile. Refused while a person or a group has it attached or as a ceiling. Needs a confirmation.

document.desc: The profile: {"version": 1, "name", "rules": [{"id", "decision": "allow"|"deny", "operations": [...], "targets": [...], "when": {...}}]}. Saving a name that exists makes a new version (up to 5 are kept).

access.profiles.set.desc: Creates a custom profile or saves a new version of it. Refused if it would leave an administrator unable to use access.*. Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps the profile before and after.

access.profiles.validate.desc: Dry run of access.profiles.set: runs the same checks (profile, reserved names, limits, a deny of a stop, an administrator left without access) on the state the save would produce and answers the same errors, plus warnings. Writes nothing, makes no version and leaves no audit row.

access.report.desc: People and keys: role, groups, locked PINs, last sign-in, age of the PIN, the last use of each capability, and each key with its last use. Reads only.

access.review.desc: The review of accesses: profiles that reach risk 4, deny rules that can never hold, profiles nobody has, people with no group and no profile, wide keys unused for 30 days, administrators without a recent sign-in. Findings with a severity (high first); changes nothing.

exclude.desc: Event types to leave out, for example ["servicio"] hides the restarts of the service.

from.desc: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (from 00:00:00) or a full date and time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

query.desc: Text searched in the description, the type and the detail of each event (the first 80 characters are used).

to.desc: End of the range, inclusive, same format; a date alone means the end of that day. Empty: the same as from.

type.desc: Only events of this exact type (for example job_start, job_end, power, config, modo, sistema). Empty: every type.

activity.clear.desc: Deletes every Activity event that matches the filter (date range, type, excluded types, text) and returns how many; cannot be undone.

id.desc: Id of the event, as returned by activity.list (rows[].id).

activity.delete.desc: Deletes one event of the Activity history for good.

exclude.desc: Event types to leave out, for example ["servicio"] hides the restarts of the service.

from.desc: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (from 00:00:00) or a full date and time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

mine.desc: true: only the events of the person of this session (the server knows who it is); without users (open mode) it filters nothing.

query.desc: Text searched in the description, the type and the detail of each event (the first 80 characters are used).

to.desc: End of the range, inclusive, same format; a date alone means the end of that day. Empty: the same as from.

type.desc: Only events of this exact type (for example job_start, job_end, power, config, modo, sistema). Empty: every type.

user.desc: Only the events done by this person (user name, as in rows[].user).

activity.list.desc: Lists the events of the Activity history (jobs, power, configuration, warnings...) of a date range, paged and filtered; also returns the total and the event types that exist.

points.desc: safety_check: ids of the checklist points the operator confirmed (at most 20, each up to 40 characters).

text.desc: Text of the event as shown in Activity and in the notification (cut at 300 characters). Required except for safety_check; for job_start it is the name of the job.

type.desc: Kind of event: calibration (a calibration was saved), config (a setting changed), warning, fire (flame or smoke seen: urgent), safety_check (the operator confirmed the manual safety checklist before a cut; the user is the caller) or job_start (the operator started a job from a page).

zone.desc: safety_check and job_start: name or number of the work zone.

activity.log.desc: Writes an event in the Activity history and, if that event type is enabled in the notifications, sends it to the phone. For things that leave no trace on the machine (calibrations, settings, warnings, fire).

exclude.desc: Event types to leave out, for example ["servicio"] hides the restarts of the service.

from.desc: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (from 00:00:00) or a full date and time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

mine.desc: true: only the events of the person of this session (the server knows who it is); without users (open mode) it filters nothing.

to.desc: End of the range, inclusive, same format; a date alone means the end of that day. Empty: the same as from.

user.desc: Only the events done by this person (user name, as in rows[].user).

activity.summary.desc: Summary of the Activity history of a date range: events per type, jobs started / finished / cancelled, total job time and kWh, the finished jobs (newest first, up to 30), the last failures and emergency stops (up to 8) and the first and last event.

on.desc: true enables the automatic mode, false leaves the pump under manual control only.

air.auto.desc: Turns the automatic air assist on or off: when on, the pump follows the laser codes M3/M4 (on) and M5 (off after the delay of air.delay). Saved; the current pump state is not changed.

seconds.desc: Delay in seconds after M5, 0 to 60.

air.delay.desc: Sets how many seconds the automatic air assist waits after M5 before switching the pump off. Saved.

on.desc: true switches the pump on, false switches it off.

air.set.desc: Switches the air assist pump on or off now by running the macro laser/airon.g or laser/airoff.g (they only act in Laser mode) and updates the state shown on the pages.

lang.desc: Language of the texts (es or en); without it the English of the code.

after.desc: Id of the last row of the previous page (0 = from the start).

from.desc: Start (YYYY-MM-DD or full date and time); default today.

to.desc: End, same format; default the same day.

audit.export.desc: Exports audit rows as JSON lines with the hash of each one (`jsonl`); `done` false means call again with after = next_after.

denied.desc: Only the refusals (no permission or no session).

detail.desc: Add to each row the detail of the event (profile and rule that decided, target, decision, duration) when it has one.

from.desc: Start (YYYY-MM-DD or full date and time); default today.

group.desc: Only the people who belong to this access group now.

op.desc: Only operations starting with this text.

result.desc: Only allowed, denied (refused by the access rules or no session) or error calls.

to.desc: End, same format; default the same day.

audit.list.desc: Reads the audit: who did what, from which device. It cannot be changed or deleted from the API.

settings.desc: What to change: reads {camera, audit, config: bool}, alarms {access_damaged, denial_burst, sensitive_change, chain_broken: bool}, read_sample, read_daily_cap, burst_threshold, burst_window_s, alarm_quiet_s. Without it only reads.

audit.settings.desc: Reads or changes the settings of the audit: optional read events (off by default), their sampling and daily cap, and the alarms.

after.desc: Id of the last link of the previous call (0 = from the start).

limit.desc: Most links to look at in this call.

audit.verify.desc: Verifies the chain of hashes of the audit. Answers ok with the number of links, or the first broken row and why; `done` false means call again with after = next_after. A row older than the chain is outside it.

args.desc: The arguments the call would carry (they can escalate it).

operation.desc: An operation name (or <ns>:<name>). Or give operations.

operations.desc: Instead of operation: up to 100 items, each an operation name or an object with operation, target and args.

target.desc: workshop:<plugin>:<type>/<id> (no wildcard). Left out: the target the call would declare.

auth.can.desc: Would the CALLER be allowed this operation (and target) now: allowed, and the cause (code, and the profile, rule and ceiling by name, never their contents). Only about the person making the call: it takes no person. A stop is always allowed. Any role, any session.

new_pin.desc: New PIN: 6 to 12 digits, not a run (345678), a repetition (454545), a probable date or a common PIN; PINs already saved keep working.

auth.change_pin.desc: The logged in person changes their own PIN.

auth.keepalive.desc: The person is still there: postpones the expiry of the session (send on real use, at most once a minute).

name.desc: Name of the person (1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots or hyphens).

auth.login.desc: Identifies a person. Answers a token to send in the header X-Workshop-Token (with an id of the browser in X-Workshop-Device). Too many wrong PINs lock the user for a while.

auth.logout.desc: Ends the session of the token sent.

token.desc: Session token of a browser (the header X-Workshop-Token it sent).

auth.resolve.desc: For local programs (the Vision server): who a browser's session token is, to apply the roles to the calls the page makes to them directly. Needs the local key; for a DWC session it is an administrator's operation.

auth.whoami.desc: Who the caller is, the role, and the permission table (operation -> lowest role) the pages use to hide what the role cannot do.

beds.desc: Bed numbers (the P of M140) of the zones in the order they are to be used, edges first (the page computes it from the map).

hold_min.desc: Minutes the zones stay at temperature once they arrive, then they are turned off (0 to 60; default 15).

only.desc: Bed numbers to tune, a subset of beds (default all of them): the others of beds are the neighbours that are held or turned off.

stagger_s.desc: Seconds between two zone starts (0 to 600; default 30).

together.desc: true (default): the other zones are held at the working temperature while one is tuned; false: they are off.

bedcal.plan.desc: What a preheat or a tuning of the bed zones would do, WITHOUT sending anything: the zones with their heater, cap, offset and target, the lines in the order they are sent (all from the closed G-code list) and the lines that turn everything off. Refused (reason bedcal_*) when the machine is not idle, a zone has no heater of its own, a heater is in fault or a temperature is over the zone maximum or the heater cap.

beds.desc: Bed numbers (the P of M140) of the zones in the order they are to be used, edges first (the page computes it from the map).

hold_min.desc: Minutes the zones stay at temperature once they arrive, then they are turned off (0 to 60; default 15).

stagger_s.desc: Seconds between two zone starts (0 to 600; default 30).

bedcal.preheat.desc: HEATS the bed zones: starts them in the order given, one every stagger_s seconds (M140 P<bed> S<temp + offset>), waits until they arrive, holds them hold_min minutes and turns them off. Needs the confirmation of level 3, the technician role, an idle machine and no other procedure; it is a procedure of machine.run (machine.runs, bedcal.status). bedcal.stop turns every zone off. Answers {run_id, kind, state}.

bedcal.status.desc: The bed calibration run in progress or the last one: {active, run: {id, kind, state, phase, step, total, user, params, error {code}, result: {zones: [{bed, heater, target, current, state, result, error, model, model_line}], phase, off, elapsed_s}} | null}.

bedcal.stop.desc: Stops the heating or tuning of the bed zones in progress and turns EVERY configured zone off at once (M140 P<bed> S-273.15). Never blocked, any role, no login.

beds.desc: Bed numbers (the P of M140) of the zones in the order they are to be used, edges first (the page computes it from the map).

only.desc: Bed numbers to tune, a subset of beds (default all of them): the others of beds are the neighbours that are held or turned off.

together.desc: true (default): the other zones are held at the working temperature while one is tuned; false: they are off.

bedcal.tune.desc: TUNES the PID of each bed zone in the order given (M303 H<heater> S<temp>), one at a time, alone or with the neighbours held at the working temperature; the new model stays in use on the board (save it with machine.config.plan kind config.heater_model). Needs the confirmation of level 4, the technician role, an idle machine and no other procedure; opens an active risk. bedcal.stop turns every zone off. Answers {run_id, kind, state}.

bedestimates.get.desc: The optional data of the bed power estimate and the insulation test: {inputs, insulation: {before, after}, rev}.

bedestimates.set.desc: Saves the optional data of the estimate and the runs of the insulation test (the whole value). It touches no heater.

bedzones.get.desc: The configuration of the bed zones (enabled, zones with their bed number, active flag and offset, maximum temperature, maximum offset, tolerance, M190 timeout, map layout), its revision, the problems found in the saved file (the zones are then not used) and the bed heater slots the board reports: {config, rev, problems, detected: [{bed, heater}]}.

bedzones.off.desc: Turns every configured zone off (M140 P<bed> S-273.15), active or not. Never blocked. Returns the codes sent.

base_rev.desc: The rev returned by bedzones.get ("0" for a file that does not exist yet).

bedzones.set.desc: Validates and saves the bed zones configuration only if nobody changed it since base_rev; otherwise error 'conflict' with error.current. Invalid fields answer invalid_args with one message per field. While enabled is false M140 / M190 go through to the firmware untouched.

temperature.desc: Setpoint in C; 0 turns off. With no zone it is the global setpoint (each active zone gets it plus its offset).

zone.desc: Bed number of ONE zone to set by hand (no offset added); omit it for all the active zones.

bedzones.setpoint.desc: HEATS the bed: sends M140 P<bed> S<setpoint> to the zones. A setpoint over the configured maximum, an offset over its limit or an unknown zone is refused and nothing is sent. Returns the codes sent.

data.desc: {archivo, T: {giro, tx, ty} design to bed, area: {xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax}, hechas: [T of each part already cut]}.

bigpart.counts.desc: Big part wizard: counts how the job splits into parts for the given placement and cutting area.

data.desc: {diseno: [[x, y], ...] marks in the design, cama: [[x, y], ...] the same marks measured on the bed}.

bigpart.fit.desc: Big part wizard: computes the rotation and offset of the material from the marks measured on the bed.

data.desc: {archivo, T, area, hechas, corr: [x, y] laser offset, pct: laser power 1-30 % (default 8), vel: feed 100-6000 (default 800)}.

bigpart.marks.desc: Big part wizard: chooses where the registration crosses go and writes the job 0:/sys/workshop/gcodes/big-part-marks.gcode. Never moves.

data.desc: {archivo, T, area, hechas, corr: [x, y] laser offset, n: number of the part (default 1)}.

bigpart.part.desc: Big part wizard: writes the job of one part to 0:/sys/workshop/gcodes/big-part-piece.gcode. Never moves (the page starts the job).

data.desc: {archivo: path of the job file}. Request of the page as an object (see the operation); errors come back as {ok: false, error}.

bigpart.read.desc: Big part wizard: reads a job file and returns its summary; writes the drawing to 0:/sys/workshop/data/big-part.json. Never moves.

blackbox.hide.desc: Hides the card with the report of the last unclean shutdown of the system.

blackbox.lines.desc: Returns the last lines written by the black box, as text.

blackbox.note.desc: Writes a note event in the black box (for example from a macro, to mark a moment).

blackbox.show.desc: Shows again the card with the report of the last unclean shutdown of the system (the report is never deleted).

blackbox.status.desc: State of the black box (a line of load, CPU, RAM, temperature and state every few seconds in 0:/sys/workshop/data/blackbox/) and the report of the last unclean shutdown.

bridge.service.desc: State of the G-code bridge unit of this Pi: installed, running, starts with the Pi, and if this service may start / stop it.

on.desc: true: start the bridge and make it start with the Pi (it survives a power cut); false: stop it and do not start it again.

bridge.service.set.desc: Starts or stops the bridge of this Pi (systemctl through one sudoers rule limited to that unit). Stopping is refused while a live job is open.

line.desc: BRIDGE HELP / STATUS / LIST / NAME or a query G-code of the bridge list (M114, M115, M119...).

bridge.test.desc: Sends one query line to the G-code bridge through a short local connection and returns its answer; anything that moves is refused.

camera.desc: Id of the camera; empty: the main camera (main).

camera.burst.desc: Takes several dated photos in a row from a camera; they are made in the background and appear in the captures.

camera.desc: Id of the camera; empty: the main camera (main).

camera.capture.desc: Takes a photo from a camera and saves it with the date in the captures folder (0:/workshop/camera/captures).

url.desc: Stream address starting with http:// or https://, for example http://192.168.1.50:81/stream.

camera.detect.desc: Asks a camera on the local network whether it is an ESP32-camera and whether it has a flash: {ok, reachable, esp32, flash, framesize}. reachable false means the camera did not answer (busy, Wi-Fi drop), which says nothing about what it is. Public and link-local addresses are refused.

file.desc: File name of a timelapse video.

since.desc: Seconds from the start of the video where the new one starts.

until.desc: Seconds where it ends (empty: to the end).

camera.edit.desc: Makes a NEW video from a timelapse, trimmed and with another speed; the original stays. It is assembled in the background.

camera.desc: Id of the camera; empty: the main camera (main).

on.desc: true switches the flash on, false switches it off.

camera.flash.desc: Switches the flash of a camera on or off: the LED of the ESP32-camera or the work lights, as the flash_source of that camera says. The service remembers it (camera.status: flash {capable, on}) and switches it off by itself when nobody looks at the camera any more or after 10 minutes. Answers {ok, camera, flash} or {ok: false, error}.

camera.desc: Id of the camera; empty: the main camera (main).

camera.image.get.desc: The image settings of an ESP32-camera: what is saved for it (profile, fine values, auto), what the camera says now (live: its own /status, null if it does not answer), the profile that fits the machine now (suggested), the profiles with their values and the resolutions of its firmware ({name, number, width, height}). Answers {ok: false, error} for a camera that is not an ESP32-camera.

auto.desc: true: the service switches to the profile that fits what the machine is doing (laser job: cut, else balanced).

camera.desc: Id of the camera; empty: the main camera (main).

profile.desc: A profile: it is applied, saved and the fine values are dropped.

settings.desc: Fine values over the profile, for example {"brightness": 1, "framesize": "SVGA"} (framesize by name: QVGA, CIF, VGA, SVGA, XGA, HD, SXGA).

camera.image.set.desc: Applies image settings to an ESP32-camera and saves them in camera.json for every screen. The service applies them again by itself when the camera restarts, which resets it. Nothing is saved when the camera did not take them. Answers like camera.image.get.

file.desc: File name of a capture or a timelapse.

value.desc: true: it is never deleted by itself (the caps skip it); false: it counts again.

camera.keep.desc: Marks or unmarks a capture or a timelapse as kept, and checks the caps again.

file.desc: File name of a capture (.jpg) or a timelapse (.mp4 / .mov), as listed by the relay.

camera.remove.desc: Deletes a capture or a timelapse video with what travels with it (thumbnail, data, kept stills). It stays in the audit with who asked.

file.desc: File name of a capture or a timelapse.

camera.rename.desc: Changes the visible name of a capture or a timelapse (the file keeps its name).

cfg.desc: The look to apply over the one the video was made with (the keys of a timelapse take: codec, framing, grade, speed...).

file.desc: File name of a timelapse video whose stills were kept.

camera.rerender.desc: Makes a NEW video from the stills kept with a timelapse, with another look; the original stays. It is assembled in the background.

action.desc: schedule: record from a time to a time; unschedule: forget the schedule.

since.desc: Start, epoch seconds (empty: now, when until is given).

camera.schedule.desc: Schedules a timelapse to start and / or stop at a time, or removes the schedule. It is kept across restarts.

changes.desc: Settings to change, with the names of a read (for example {"notice_drop": true} or {"timelapse": {"each_s": 10}}). Empty: only read.

camera.service.desc: Reads or changes the camera service settings (warning when a camera stops answering, limits of captures and timelapses, timelapse options). Without changes it only reads; with changes it saves them.

camera.start.desc: Starts the camera relay again; fails without a configured camera. Not saved: after a restart the saved setting applies.

camera.status.desc: State of the camera relay (the process that serves the camera stream to the screens), with the number of viewers and the list of cameras (cameras.json: id, name, address, photo, esp32, relay, flash_source, open and via_relay, which says whether the relay serves that camera) and cameras_rev, the revision of that file.

camera.stop.desc: Stops the camera relay: the stream is cut for every screen watching it. Not saved: after a restart the saved setting applies.

action.desc: start, stop, or status (default: only returns the state).

cfg.desc: Settings of this take when starting (the keys of the timelapse settings of camera.service: cameras, each_s, fps, armed...); the rest come from the service settings.

name.desc: Name of the timelapse when starting (default "Timelapse HH:MM").

camera.timelapse.desc: Starts or stops a manual timelapse recording, or returns its state. Starting fails if one is already recording or less than 2 GB are free.

camera.token.desc: Returns the key of the day (valid today and tomorrow) to watch the relay from another screen when DWC has a password.

refresh.desc: true reads the board again instead of using the answer cached for 30 seconds.

capabilities.get.desc: What this machine has, discovered from the live board and the SD: board and firmware, axes with their range, boards and driver chips, tools, heaters, fans, probe, modes, laser, spindle, extruder, LED strip, cameras, meter and light scenes. Each capability has present (true/false) and source (discovered, declared or default). Works with a plain config.g; nothing of the workshop is assumed.

comms.get.desc: Returns the channel the service uses to send its G-codes to the board and the one of the jog moves, with warnings and suggestions.

jog_channel.desc: Channel of the G1 moves of the jog: auto (Aux2 if free, else SBC), Aux2, Aux or SBC.

plugin_channel.desc: Channel of the codes of the service: auto, Aux2, Aux or SBC.

comms.set.desc: Advanced: changes the channel of the service codes and/or of the jog. Refused with a job, recent bridge activity, a jog gesture or the free jog on, and for channels that cannot be chosen now. Saved, applies at once, logged in Activity; level 4 confirmation.

checks.desc: Expected after the restart, for example {placas: [1, 40], ejes: 4, calentadores: 2, sondas: 1} (boards, axes, heaters, probes).

file.desc: 0:/ path of a JSON file on the SD with the checks (instead of checks).

id.desc: Id of the copy to go back to. Use this or tx.

seconds.desc: Time to confirm after the restart, in seconds (default 300; the service keeps it between 30 and 3600).

tx.desc: Transaction of the commit; the copy made before it is used. Use this or id.

who.desc: Who does it (person or screen); noted in the roll back state and in Activity.

config.arm.desc: Arms the automatic roll back before restarting the board with a new configuration: on a startup error, halt, no reconnection, a failed check or no confirmation in time, the copy is restored and the board restarted (with a notice). Refused with a job running.

owner.desc: Id of the screen that holds the save lock; refused if another screen holds it.

tx.desc: Id of the staged transaction (0:/sys/workshop/data/config-staging/<tx>/ with its manifest.json).

config.commit.desc: Saves every file staged by a screen in one go: checks the lock and the hashes, copies the current files to the history first, then replaces them all atomically (put back if it fails half way). Logged in Activity.

who.desc: Who does it (person or screen); noted in the roll back state and in Activity.

config.confirm.desc: Confirms that the new configuration works and disarms the roll back.

id.desc: Id of the copy (YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS, as returned by config.list).

config.get.desc: Returns the manifest of one copy of the configuration history (its files and why it was made).

config.guard.desc: Returns the state of the roll back (armed or not, deadline, last result), the same as the plugin data configGuard.

config.list.desc: Lists the copies of the configuration history, newest first (id, date, reason, who, files).

owner.desc: Id of the screen that takes the lock.

seconds.desc: How long the lock lasts (default 120); the service keeps it between 10 and 600 seconds.

who.desc: Name shown to the other screens while the lock is held.

config.lock.desc: Takes or renews the save lock of the configuration for one screen, so two screens never save at once; refused while another screen holds it.

id.desc: Id of the copy to restore (from config.list).

owner.desc: Id of the screen; refused if another screen holds the save lock.

reboot.desc: true restarts the board (M999) to load the restored files.

seconds.desc: Above 0: arms the roll back to the copy of the current files with this time to confirm; 0 disarms an armed roll back.

who.desc: Who does it (person or screen); noted in the roll back state and in Activity.

config.restore.desc: Restores any copy of the history (the current files are copied first; files the copy did not have are deleted). Refused with a job running; can arm the roll back and restart the board.

who.desc: Who does it (person or screen); noted in the roll back state and in Activity.

config.rollback.desc: Emergency exit: restores the armed copy now and restarts the board, without looking at the save lock.

data.desc: Request: {archivos: [SD paths such as sys/config.g], motivo, quien, rrf, modo}; a plain list of paths works too. Use this or file.

file.desc: 0:/ path of a JSON file on the SD with the same request (for long lists). Use this or data.

mode.desc: Machine mode noted in the manifest (for example Laser, CNC, FFF); overrides modo.

reason.desc: Reason shown in the history (overrides motivo; default "Copia manual").

rrf.desc: RepRapFirmware version noted in the manifest; overrides rrf.

who.desc: Who made the copy (person or screen); overrides quien.

config.snapshot.desc: Copies a set of configuration files of the SD to the configuration history (0:/sys/workshop/config-history/<id>/ with a manifest); missing files are listed as absent. Returns the id of the copy.

owner.desc: Id of the screen that holds the lock.

config.unlock.desc: Releases the save lock; only its owner can, except an expired lock, which anyone can release.

db.backup.desc: Makes a backup now: the database and the workshop folders (0:/sys/workshop config, data, zones) in one .tar.gz in the backup folder (and in the extra copy if set).

db.delete_previous.desc: Deletes the backups of the previous backup folder that already have a copy in the current one; the others are left alone.

path.desc: Absolute folder on the system card (inside the DSF SD folder) or on a USB stick (/media/..., /mnt/...), for example one of db.places.

db.folder.desc: Changes the backup folder: the existing backups are copied (not moved) and checked; the old folder stays until db.delete_previous.

file.desc: File name of the backup in the backup folder (as listed by db.status).

keep.desc: true (default) protects it from the automatic deletion; false lets the rotation delete it again.

db.keep.desc: Marks a backup so the rotation never deletes it automatically, or releases that mark.

db.places.desc: Lists where backups can be kept: the system card and every mounted USB stick, with their free space.

auto.desc: Automatic daily backups on or off.

daily.desc: How many daily backups are kept (the service keeps it between 1 and 60).

extra_copy.desc: Extra copy of each backup: "auto" (the first USB stick, or the card when the main folder is a stick), "no", or a folder on the card or on a stick.

summarize.desc: Summarize meter readings older than 90 days to one per hour (after a warning and a backup); false never summarizes.

weekly.desc: How many weekly backups are kept among the older ones (0 to 52).

db.settings.desc: Changes the backup settings; only the arguments given change. Returns the resulting settings.

db.status.desc: Returns the state of the service database, its backups and its maintenance.

from.desc: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (from 00:00:00) or a full date and time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

meter.desc: Key of the meter (empty: the main one, the one that feeds the system); "total" adds up the meters on their own line.

to.desc: End of the range, inclusive, same format; a date alone means the end of that day. Empty: the same as from.

energy.history.desc: Returns the energy meter readings of a date range, paged, with a summary (kWh, peak and average power) and the power series of the range.

date.desc: Reference date YYYY-MM-DD (default today): its day, month or year is used.

meter.desc: Key of the meter (empty: the main one, the one that feeds the system); "total" adds up the meters on their own line.

period.desc: day (its 24 hours, default), month (its days) or year (its months).

energy.period.desc: Returns the kWh of a meter per hour of a day, per day of a month or per month of a year, ready to draw bars.

energy.rate_get.desc: Returns the currency and the price of one kWh used to show the approximate cost of the energy.

currency.desc: Currency code shown next to the costs, for example USD, EUR, MXN (only a label; empty: the currency of the machine profile, or none).

value.desc: Price of one kWh in that currency.

energy.rate_set.desc: Saves the currency and the price of one kWh (a label and a number, no conversion). Logged in Activity.

file.desc: Destination (relative to 0:/) of one example to create again even if it was created before; without it only the examples never created are made.

plugin.desc: Id of the plugin that offers the examples.

examples.create.desc: Creates the example files of a plugin that are missing and were never created. It never overwrites a file.

plugin.desc: Id of the plugin that offers the examples (for example WorkshopJog).

examples.list.desc: Lists the example files a plugin offers (commented macros to edit) with their state: configured, example (all commented, still to configure) or missing.

mode.desc: puntero: the machine moves with the laser off; laser: the laser is on at power_pct.

points.desc: Corners of the frame as [[x, y], ...] in MACHINE coordinates of the head (G53), closed (the last point is the first); 2 to 400 points.

power_pct.desc: Laser power in % (1 to 10), only with mode laser.

repeat.desc: Times it goes around: 1 = once (default), N = N times, 0 = until frame.stop.

frame.start.desc: Traces a frame with the machine WITHOUT making a job: the service sends short pieces and keeps little queued, so frame.stop works within about a second. Refused with a job, a live job or the jog moving; with the laser it needs Laser mode, X and Y homed and at most 10 %, and every declared interlock (lid, extraction, key) closed: error interlock_open otherwise.

frame.status.desc: State of the frame: active, mode, lap, how many laps, how it ended and the error if any.

frame.stop.desc: Stops the frame in progress (never refused). The laser goes off; what was already queued on the board finishes (about a second).

file.desc: One file; without it the whole cache is cleared.

gcodelib.forget.desc: Deletes cache entries: {removed}. With auto_index on, the files are read again by the worker.

file.desc: Path of the G-code file, e.g. 0:/gcodes/part.gcode (inside the SD; .g .gcode .gco .nc .gc .ngc .tap).

gcodelib.info.desc: Everything the library knows about one file: {state: ready, summary, header, temps, layers_table, types} or {state: pending | working | error}. A file that is not read yet is queued first in line.

detail.desc: low = fewer points (0.3 mm), normal = 0.05 mm and the travel moves.

file.desc: Path of the G-code file, e.g. 0:/gcodes/part.gcode (inside the SD; .g .gcode .gco .nc .gc .ngc .tap).

gcodelib.layers.desc: The path of a window of layers: {from, to, total, types, plane: 3d | 2d, layers: [{layer, z (null in 2d), name? (2d), segments: {type: [[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]]}, travel?}], truncated}. An answer holds about 400 KB: when it is cut, `to` is the last layer sent and truncated is true.

kind.desc: Only these kinds: fff | laser | cnc | travel | unknown (a list or a comma separated string).

query.desc: Text the name or a tag must contain.

gcodelib.list.desc: The G-code files of a folder joined with the library cache: {dir, dirs, rows: [{name, path, size, modified, state: ready | pending | working | error, error?, summary?}], total, pending, cache_bytes, counts: {fff, laser, cnc, travel, unknown}}. It never parses: files without a cache entry are queued for the background worker.

file.desc: One file to read again; without it the folder is scanned.

gcodelib.refresh.desc: Reads a file again (its entry is dropped and it goes first), or scans the watched folders for new, changed and deleted files: {queued}.

file.desc: Path of the G-code file, e.g. 0:/gcodes/part.gcode (inside the SD; .g .gcode .gco .nc .gc .ngc .tap).

gcodelib.thumbnail.desc: {width, height, png_base64, synthetic?}, the embedded thumbnail or else a small one drawn from the toolpath (synthetic: true); {none: true} when there is nothing to draw, or {state: pending | working | error}.

action.desc: notify = only warn loudly when a fire or servo protection is down during a laser or CNC job (default); pause = also pause a file job.

enabled.desc: Turn the guard on or off (default on).

external_tolerance_s.desc: Seconds without a sign of life before Vision or RS485 count as down (default 30).

grace_s.desc: Extra seconds for the first heartbeat after a start or restart (default 60).

renotify_s.desc: Debounce: the phone is not warned again about the same protection before these seconds (default 600).

tolerance_factor.desc: An internal process is late after this many times its expected pace (default 3).

guard.set.desc: Changes the settings of the protection guard. Saved.

guard.status.desc: Returns the state of the protection guard: which safety processes are expected, which are watched, which are down (degraded), and its settings. The same watch list is published in the data key guardStatus.

limit.desc: Most points per series (default 300); the samples are averaged in buckets.

range.desc: How far back: 1h (default), 6h, 24h or 7d (the retention is 7 days by default).

since.desc: Epoch seconds, from: with it the range is a stretch from here to `until` instead of `range`.

until.desc: Epoch seconds, until (default: now); only with `since`.

health.history.desc: Returns the history of the Pi health kept by the service: series cpu (% use), temp (C), ram (% in use), disk (% in use) and wifi (% signal, 0 when down), each a list of {t: epoch milliseconds, y: value} averaged in buckets of step_s seconds.

from.desc: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (from 00:00:00) or a full date and time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

to.desc: End of the range, inclusive, same format; a date alone means the end of that day. Empty: the same as from.

history.delete.desc: Deletes the received calls of a date range from the history; cannot be undone.

channel.desc: Only the calls of this origin channel (HTTP, SBC, Aux...); "-" for rows saved without origin data.

errors.desc: true: only the calls that failed.

from.desc: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD (from 00:00:00) or a full date and time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

kind.desc: Only the calls of this origin kind (page, console, job_file, macro, bridge, service, external...); "-" for rows without origin data.

name.desc: Only the calls of this operation, for example lights.get.

plugin.desc: Only the calls of this plugin or page tag; "-" for rows without origin data.

query.desc: Text searched in the call and in its answer.

result.desc: Only the calls with this result: ok, error or blocked; "-" for rows without origin data.

rw.desc: 0 every call, 1 only the ones that change something, 2 only reads.

to.desc: End of the range, inclusive, same format; a date alone means the end of that day. Empty: the same as from.

via.desc: Only the calls that arrived this way, as written in the history (for example "API (DWC session)", "macro", "service").

history.list.desc: Lists the API calls received by the service (origin, result, duration) of a date range, paged and filtered; also returns counters of the range and of the last hour.

job.cancel.desc: The live job was cancelled: it is closed as cancelled and logged in Activity.

job.close.desc: Closes the open live job by hand; its duration ends at its last activity.

job.end.desc: The live job ended: it is closed and its duration and kWh are logged in Activity.

job.get.desc: Returns the open live job (name, start, mode, last activity) and the idle timeout.

name.desc: Name of the job (default: "Live job" in the language of DWC; the pages show that default name in their own language).

job.start.desc: A live job starts (sent by an external program, not a file RRF sees): its start, mode, zone and energy are recorded; an open one is closed first. In Laser mode with a declared interlock (lid, extraction, key) that is not ok it fails with interlock_open.

minutes.desc: Minutes without activity, up to 1440; 0 = never.

job.timeout.desc: Sets after how many minutes without activity an open live job closes by itself. Saved.

max_vertices.desc: Most vertices of the path that come back (the numbers are exact anyway).

mode.desc: Mode used to read the file (default: the mode of the machine).

jobs.preview.desc: Reads a G-code file WITHOUT running it: the planned path in machine coordinates of the active work zone, estimated time, distances, feed range, pieces, layers, bounding box and the outline (convex hull) of what it works on.

axis.desc: Letter of an extra axis (U, V, W, A...); X, Y, Z and other values are ignored.

speed.desc: Speed in percent of the jog range, from the minimum to the maximum jog feed of the jog settings (default 50); never above the axis speed limits of the board (M203).

value.desc: Deflection, -1 to 1; the sign gives the direction.

jog.axis.desc: Moves an extra axis (U, V, W, A...) while its jog control is held (repeat while held). Same movement rules as jog.xy.

on.desc: true enters the mode, false leaves it.

jog.free.desc: Enters or leaves the jog mode without limits (moves without homing or beyond the M208 limits, guarded by stall detection); the jog loop applies the request.

release.desc: true: this device lets go of ITS control; ignored when another device holds the jog. Without it (or false) the stop stops everything, whoever holds it (safety).

jog.stop_axis.desc: The extra axis control was released: stops that jog at once. Never blocked.

release.desc: true: this device lets go of ITS control; ignored when another device holds the jog. Without it (or false) the stop stops everything, whoever holds it (safety).

jog.stop_xy.desc: The X/Y knob was released: stops the X/Y jog at once. Never blocked.

release.desc: true: this device lets go of ITS control; ignored when another device holds the jog. Without it (or false) the stop stops everything, whoever holds it (safety).

jog.stop_z.desc: The Z control was released: stops the Z jog at once. Never blocked.

speed.desc: Speed in percent of the jog range, from the minimum to the maximum jog feed of the jog settings (default 50); never above the axis speed limits of the board (M203).

x.desc: X part of the knob deflection, -1 to 1 (the length of the x, y vector sets the speed; small values are a dead zone).

y.desc: Y part of the knob deflection, -1 to 1.

jog.xy.desc: Moves X/Y while the jog knob is held: the service ramps the moves and stops if no update arrives within about 0.9 s, so repeat every ~300 ms. Denied with a job, bridge activity or a reservation; a live job idle asks a confirmation.

speed.desc: Speed in percent of the jog range, from the minimum to the maximum jog feed of the jog settings (default 50); never above the axis speed limits of the board (M203). Z uses the zRatio fraction of that feed.

z.desc: Deflection of the Z control, -1 to 1; the sign gives the direction.

jog.z.desc: Moves Z while the jog control is held (repeat while held, like jog.xy). Same movement rules as jog.xy.

level.desc: Lowest level shown: all (default), notice, warning or error (that level and the worse ones).

lines.desc: Most lines returned (default 200); the last ones are kept.

noise.desc: hide (default) leaves out a few known harmless lines (Wi-Fi driver frames, a .NET Wi-Fi 7 warning, AppArmor profiles loaded at boot); show keeps them, flagged noise.

search.desc: Text the line (or its program name) must contain, any case; it is data, never passed to a program.

unit.desc: Which log: a Duet or workshop unit, NetworkManager, ssh, the kernel, or the workshop's own files: workshop-service (the service log) and install (the start-up runs). Default duetcontrolserver.

journal.read.desc: Reads the system journal of one unit of a closed list (or the kernel), or one of the workshop's own logs, read-only. Returns {readable, lines: [{t: epoch ms, p: 0-7, who, text, noise?}], truncated, noise_hidden}; when the service cannot read the journal, {readable: false, reason: no_permission | failed | no_journalctl | no_file}.

days.desc: Valid for this many days, up to 3650 (empty or 0: does not expire).

deny.desc: Operations always refused, even if a class or a capability allows them: names, patterns and cap:<id>. Denying wins.

kinds.desc: Operation classes allowed: read, write, motion, stop, power (admin can never be given).

name.desc: Name of the service that will use the key (unique).

ops.desc: Operations also allowed: names, patterns such as light.* and capabilities as cap:<id> (ids in roles.list; never an administration or non-delegable one).

preset.desc: Starting permissions (see keys.list); kinds and ops given replace the ones of the preset.

keys.create.desc: Creates an access key for an external service; the key is returned only once and goes in the X-Workshop-Key header. Needs a confirmation.

keys.list.desc: Lists the access keys of external services (name, permissions, allowed_ops = the operations each may call, expiry, use; never the keys themselves), the presets and the classes.

keys.preview.desc: What a key with these permissions could call (allowed_ops), with the entries as they would be saved; nothing is created. Same rule as every call with a key.

id.desc: Id of the key (from keys.list).

keys.revoke.desc: Deletes a key for good: the service that used it stops working at once. Needs a confirmation.

days.desc: New validity in days from now, up to 3650; 0: never expires; not given: unchanged.

deny.desc: New list of refused operations: names, patterns and cap:<id> (replaces the old one).

enabled.desc: false suspends the key without deleting it; true enables it again.

id.desc: Id of the key (from keys.list).

kinds.desc: New list of allowed operation classes (replaces the old one).

ops.desc: New list of allowed operations: names, patterns and cap:<id> (replaces the old one).

keys.update.desc: Changes the name, permissions, expiry or enabled state of a key; only the arguments given change.

file.desc: File name of the job it is armed for (job.file.fileName).

layerrecipes.arm.desc: ARMS a recipe for ONE job file (in memory, off by default, dropped after an hour if the job never starts): while that job is printing, the service sends M568 P<tool> S... (extruder track) and M140 P<bed> S<t> for each listed zone (bed track) when the layer changes, inside the limits of the recipe and of each heater. It never switches a heater on or off. A pause holds; cancel, end or a lost job disarm it and leave the temperatures as they are; a board that refuses a code turns that track off. The bed track needs the bed zones enabled with all its zones defined. `conflict` while another recipe, or a pellet profile (when the recipe has an extruder track), is armed.

layerrecipes.disarm.desc: Stops applying the recipe now and leaves the temperatures as they are. Never blocked.

layerrecipes.get.desc: One recipe: {name, recipe: {format: 2, kind: pellet|filament, material, note, tracks: {extruder?, bed?}}, rev}. The points of a track are DELTAS over the G-code.

layerrecipes.import_pellet.desc: Copies every pellet profile that has no recipe of the same name as an extruder-only recipe, as deltas over the profile's first point. Nothing is replaced; the profiles stay.

layerrecipes.list.desc: The temperature-by-layer recipes: {recipes: [{name, kind, material, tracks, axis, points}], rev}.

flat.desc: Instead of a saved recipe, a FLAT one built on the fly for a material without layers: {extruder?: {tool, heaters, temps}, bed?: {zones, temps}}, absolute temperatures per zone (already staggered by the caller). Nothing is saved.

layerrecipes.preview.desc: Transparency preview, read-only: reads the G-code file and returns what the recipe WOULD send, layer by layer, with the same planner and limits as the armed run: {name, file, layers, axis, truncated, notes: [{key, params, message}], changes: [{layer, z, line, at, extruder: {temps, code, limited} | null, bed: {temps, codes, limited} | null, context: [{n, text, mark}], file, conflicts, delta, base}], file_temps, layers_table}. Temperatures are base (the file's, else the board's) + delta, resolved; with `flat` the base is the material's own temperatures (delta 0) and the answer adds flat: true. It never modifies the file nor sends anything.

layerrecipes.set.desc: Validates and saves one recipe (creates or replaces it). Saving never heats anything. Invalid fields answer invalid_args with one message per field.

layerrecipes.status.desc: The armed recipe run: {armed, phase, recipe, file, layer, key, tracks: {extruder?: {applied, base, next, limited, overridden, overridden_layer}, bed?: {...}}, changes, reason}. phase: off, waiting, waiting_heat, waiting_layer, running, holding, ended.

on.desc: true switches the working light on, false switches it off.

light.set.desc: Switches the working light (lighting zone of the LED strip) on or off by running light/lighton.g or light/lightoff.g; updates the state shown on the pages.

data.desc: Optional values to try without saving: {tipo: barra|parpadeo|centro|arcoiris, color: {r, u, b, w}, paso: 1-60}.

lights.animation.desc: Runs the start-up animation of the strip now (sys/ledstartup.g), with the saved values or with the ones given. Needs a physical strip.

strip.desc: E number of the strip (the E<n> of its M950 line); empty: the main strip.

total.desc: New number of LEDs of the strip, 1 to 400.

lights.apply_m950.desc: Changes the LED count (U<total>) of the M950 line of a strip in sys/config.g, keeping a copy of config.g; the board must be restarted for it to apply. Logged in Activity; needs a confirmation.

lights.get.desc: Returns the configuration of the LED strip, lights and states (zones, colours, effects, scenes, night dimming) and its current state.

seconds.desc: How long the LEDs stay like that, 2 to 30 seconds (default 6); the automatic lighting is paused meanwhile.

segments.desc: Optional [[r, g, b, count], ...] in strip order (what the page shows, even unsaved); the rest of the strip goes off.

strip.desc: E number of the strip (the E<n> of its M950 line); empty: the main strip.

lights.identify.desc: Paints every zone of a strip in its own colour for a few seconds (or the segments given), to see where each zone is. Needs a physical strip.

data.desc: The profile exported by the page (or {config: <profile>}).

hardware.desc: true also takes the hardware layout of the profile (strips, zones); false keeps the one of this machine.

lights.import.desc: Checks a lighting profile exported by the page and returns it merged with the current configuration; nothing is saved (use lights.save).

lights.pi_pins.desc: Lists the GPIO 2 to 27 of the Pi with what each one is doing (free, in use and by what) and what the lights can do with it (a strip over SPI on a MOSI pin), plus the state of that output.

pin.desc: GPIO of the strip to test (it must be saved with its output on that pin).

lights.pi_test.desc: Shows a short test on a strip whose output is a pin of the Pi (a moving colour). The normal frame comes back by itself.

data.desc: {cuadros: [[[r,u,b,w,count], ...], ...], intervalo: 0.15-5 s, segundos: 1-20} for frames, or {simular: {config, activos, progreso, modo, trabajando}, segundos} to simulate states.

lights.preview.desc: Shows example frames on the status zone for a few seconds, or simulates states with unsaved settings; nothing is saved. Needs a physical strip.

config.desc: The lights configuration object of the page (the keys of lights.get; unknown keys are ignored).

lights.save.desc: Saves the lights configuration (validated first), writes 0:/sys/workshop/macros/system/lights.g and runs it so the board uses it. Logged in Activity.

color.desc: Free colour {r, u, b, w, p} instead of a scene.

scene.desc: Id of a saved scene of the working light (ignored when color is given).

lights.scene.desc: Sets the colour of the working light from a scene or a free colour, saves it and switches the working light on. Needs a physical strip.

on.desc: true enables the night dimming, false disables it.

lights.schedule.desc: Turns the night dimming of the lights on or off (saved).

count.desc: How many LEDs to light from the start, 1 to 400 (default: the whole strip).

seconds.desc: How long the LEDs stay like that, 2 to 30 seconds (default 6); the automatic lighting is paused meanwhile.

strip.desc: E number of the strip (the E<n> of its M950 line); empty: the main strip.

lights.test.desc: Lights the first N LEDs of a strip in blue for a few seconds, to count them. Needs a physical strip.

data.desc: Optional {color, effect} to try instead of the saved ones.

outputs.desc: Outputs: strip, screen and/or board (default: the ones enabled for that state; strip is dropped without a strip).

seconds.desc: How long it is shown, 2 to 20 seconds (default 6).

state.desc: Id of the state in the lights configuration (for example parada, pausado).

lights.test_state.desc: Shows one light state for a few seconds on the chosen outputs, optionally with another colour or effect.

index.desc: Position of the extra zone in its strip's list of extra zones, from 0.

on.desc: true switches the zone on, false switches it off.

strip.desc: Id of an additional strip; empty: the main strip.

lights.zone.desc: Switches one extra zone of the strip on or off now (saved; the strip is repainted).

id.desc: Id of the interrupted job (livejob.interrupted.list).

livejob.interrupted.discard.desc: Forgets an interrupted job (its record is deleted).

id.desc: Id of the interrupted job (livejob.interrupted.list).

livejob.interrupted.get.desc: One interrupted job with its path [[x, y, cut]] and bounding box in the program's coordinates, its modal state and where the head was.

hidden.desc: true: take it off the work table (it stays listed); false: put it back.

id.desc: Id of the interrupted job (livejob.interrupted.list).

livejob.interrupted.hide.desc: Takes an interrupted job off the work table, or puts it back, WITHOUT deleting its record: it stays in the list with the point where it stopped.

livejob.interrupted.list.desc: The interrupted live jobs (light) with, for each, blockers: why it cannot be resumed now (not_laser, rebooted, machine_unknown, job_running, machine_busy, not_homed, not_resumable) and can_resume. Also the progress of a resume in course.

id.desc: Id of the interrupted job (livejob.interrupted.list).

overlap_lines.desc: Go back this many lines and cut them again (a small overlap at the join); 0 = continue exactly.

livejob.resume.arm.desc: Arms ONE interrupted job (for 30 minutes): the next time the program sends the same job (BRIDGE JOB START) the bridge verifies and skips the lines already done, goes to where it stopped with the laser off and continues. Any line that differs cancels it and nothing runs. Needs the confirmation of level 3, laser mode, homed XY, the board not restarted since the stop and no job running.

livejob.resume.disarm.desc: Cancels the armed resume (the record stays).

livejob.stop_safe.desc: Stops the live job safely, without cutting power or cancelling anything: the lines that come after are refused, what the board already accepted finishes, the laser goes off, where it stopped is read and an interrupted record (line number, hash, position, modal state, path) is saved so the job can be resumed. Not the emergency stop. Fails when there is no live job or the bridge does not answer.

machine.beds.get.desc: The beds the machine has now ([{bed, heater, sensor, editable}]), the beds that only a configuration file defines (a mode file that is not loaded now), the first heater and sensor numbers nothing uses and the first free bed numbers.

spec.desc: {beds: [{bed, name?, sensor: {preset: thermistor|pt1000|thermocouple|tc-max31856|pt100|linear-analog, pin, + the fields of the type (see docs/api)}, output: {kind: dc|ssr|ssrdc|relay, pin}, max_temp}]}

machine.beds.preview.desc: The exact configuration lines the plan config.bed_heaters would write for these beds and the file they go into, or what is wrong with them (dc = straight to a bed or heater MOSFET of the board, out0..out3 only: error pin_not_mosfet on any other pin). Writes nothing.

calc.desc: steps (new = old * commanded / measured), skew (from the two diagonals of a square), backlash (from samples of lost motion) or ringing (frequency from the ripples).

save.desc: Store the result in the calibration history (kind calc.<calc>).

values.desc: steps: {axis, commanded, measured, old?}. skew: {pair XY|YZ|ZX, side, diag_sum, diag_diff}. backlash: {axis, samples: [mm], multiplier?}. ringing: {feed mm/min, ripples, distance mm}.

machine.calc.desc: Arithmetic of the calibration assistants: it sends nothing to the board. Returns the new value, the G-code line it would be, the warnings and the plan (kind + values) for machine.config.plan.

apply_now.desc: Also send the new M671 to the board so it is valid without a restart.

kind.desc: The kind of the plan (the role needed depends on it: the kinds that can hurt the hardware need an administrator).

machine.config.apply.desc: Writes a plan through config.commit (snapshot of the whole set first, sha check of every file, atomic swap), records it in the calibration history and, with apply_now, sends the M671 line. Refused with a job, a procedure running, or a file that changed since the plan. Needs a confirmation.

kind.desc: Kind of change: config.m671 (values {x: [..], y: [..], s, p, f}), config.bed (values {points: [{x, y}], k, s, passes, tol, rehome_z}), config.g31 ({k, p, x, y, z}), config.m208 (admin; {axes: {X: {min, max}}}), config.m92 (admin; {axes: {X: steps}}), config.g10 ({tool, offsets: {X, Y, Z}}), config.tool (a new tool), config.bed_heaters ({beds: [{bed, sensor, output, max_temp}]}: the sensor, heater and M140 P H of each zone of a split bed), config.bed_edit ({spec: {bed, heater?, sensor?}}: another heater / sensor number for a bed the configuration already defines), config.heater_model ({heaters: [{heater, r, k, kf, d, s, v?, b?, e?}]}: the M307 of bed heaters), config.heater_cap ({heaters: [{heater, max}]}: the M143 cap of bed heaters). The work offsets G54..G59.3 have no kind: they are the work zones of the Workbench.

machine.config.plan.desc: Builds a change of the configuration WITHOUT writing anything: finds the file (config.g or a macro it calls for M671, bed.g), returns the exact diff, the warnings, the values before and after and a plan_id valid for 15 minutes. Kinds of later phases answer not_implemented.

machine.height.get.desc: Height calibration of the tool, read only: what is saved per mode (method, fine adjustment, calibrated G31 K0 / SZP), the hooks of the mode files, the probes of the object model and what the assistants may do now.

machine.height.hook.desc: Adds the line that loads the calibration (M98 zcal.g) to the mode files that lack it, keeping a copy of each file.

base_rev.desc: The rev of the saved calibration this change is based on (machine.height.get).

changes.desc: {paper?, modes: {Laser|CNC|FFF: {method?, setting?, k0?, szp?}}}: fine adjustment -3..3 mm, k0 {p, x, y, z, date}, szp {s, r, date}; null removes k0 / szp.

machine.height.save.desc: Saves the height calibration (revisioned: a conflict returns the current value), rewrites sys/workshop/macros/zcal/zcal.g and applies it now when no job runs.

a.desc: szp: 1 drive level, 2 height vs reading.

action.desc: goto: the tool over X Y; jog: Z one step; mark: Z0 with the paper; measure: the BLTouch measures at X Y; szp: FFF scanning probe step.

paper.desc: mark: thickness of the paper / feeler gauge.

machine.height.step.desc: One step of the height assistants: reserves the movement (refused during a job) and sends the macros zcal-goto / zcal-mark / zcal-probe / zcal-szp or one relative Z step (never the laser: S0).

b.desc: Record id of the same kind.

machine.history.compare.desc: Compares two records of the same kind: the values that differ (results and inputs, with the difference b - a) and, for height maps, the difference grid with its statistics (same grid required).

id.desc: Record id.

machine.history.get.desc: One record complete, and what a restore would need: restorable, the values it can put back (before / after), the role needed and the state of the files the record wrote (clean, changed, missing).

kind.desc: Only this kind (probe.repeat, level.g32, mesh.probe, config.g31, offsets.snapshot...).

state.desc: Only records that ended like this.

machine.history.list.desc: The calibration records, newest first, with who, when, how they ended and whether they can be restored.

accept_current.desc: The files changed since the record: make the plan over the current file after looking at the three-way table.

id.desc: Record id.

kind.desc: The kind of the record (the registry asks for the administrator role from it). The service checks it against the record.

machine.history.restore.desc: Builds a PLAN that puts back the values of a configuration record (nothing is written): show its diff and send plan_id to machine.config.apply with the plan's kind. Refused with reason file_changed (and the three-way table) when a file is neither as the record left it nor as it found it, unless accept_current. An offsets.snapshot is refused with reason work_offsets_in_workbench: the work offsets are edited in the Workbench (zones).

margin.desc: Distance kept from the edge of the reach (default 5 for mesh, 0 for level).

mode.desc: mesh or level: which block of the answer is filled.

points.desc: Level: explicit probe points [{x, y}] (default: the profile's, bed.g's, else one near each leadscrew).

probe.desc: Probe index (default: the profile's, else the first real probe).

x0.desc: Mesh region, probe coordinates (all four of x0 x1 y0 y1, or none).

machine.layout.desc: Data for the bed view of the Mesh and Level pages, read only (nothing is sent to the board): the axis limits, the probe and its offsets, where the probe can reach, the leadscrews of M671, which mesh / levelling points would be taken and why one would not, and the last measurements. Reasons are codes (docs/MACHINE-LAYOUT-CONTRACT.md).

machine.led.get.desc: The LED strips the configuration declares (M950 E lines: strip number, pin, type T, number of LEDs, file and line), the first free strip number, the pins a strip may use with who uses each one, the types offered (rgbw = T2, rgb = T1) and the limits.

spec.desc: The strip as the plan config.led_strip takes it: strip (E number), pin, leds, type (rgbw or rgb, default rgbw), modes (optional).

machine.led.preview.desc: The exact configuration line the plan config.led_strip would write, the files it goes into (machine.g and, the first time, config.g), or what is wrong (a strip number or a pin already used says the file and line). Writes nothing.

machine.limits.get.desc: The M208 limits of every axis (min, max, probed, homed, position) from the object model, the endstops (type, high end, state) and where the configuration defines M208. Changing a limit is machine.config.plan config.m208 (administrator).

id.desc: Id of the item of the plan.

machine.maintenance.done.desc: Records that a maintenance item was done (who and when, in the audit) and resets it: the counters at that moment are its new zero.

machine.maintenance.get.desc: The maintenance counters (power-on hours, moving hours and ESTIMATED distance per axis and for the machine), the items of the plan with what each has used since it was last done and its status (ok, due_soon, due, overdue), and whether phone notices are on.

defaults.desc: true puts the generic default items back.

items.desc: The whole plan: [{id, label, axis, every_hours | every_km | every_days, hours_basis?}].

notify.desc: true: phone notice when an item becomes due (opt-in).

machine.maintenance.plan.set.desc: Edits the maintenance plan (saved in the machine profile) and the opt-in of the due notices. It only changes reminders.

action.desc: mark (default): the laser cross; capture: compute the correction with the pointer over the cross; clear: forget the mark.

power.desc: Laser power in percent for the mark (1 to 10, default 3).

save.desc: capture: also write the correction to the settings store laser and to the history.

machine.mark_cross.desc: Laser <-> pointer assistant on the server: marks a 4 mm cross with the laser (Laser mode, X and Y homed, at most 10 %, interlocks closed, the movement reserved) or computes the correction once the pointer is over it. The laser is always turned off at the end.

machine.mesh.clear.desc: Disables the mesh compensation (G29 S2). Refused with a job or a procedure running.

id.desc: Mesh id from machine.mesh.list: m-... of the library.

machine.mesh.delete.desc: Deletes a map of the library (never the active one on the board).

id.desc: Mesh id from machine.mesh.list: m-... of the library.

machine.mesh.get.desc: One map: metadata, validity, the grid, the values (null = not probed) and the statistics (min, max, range, mean, RMS, deviation, share over the profile thresholds, traffic light).

machine.mesh.list.desc: The library of height maps (newest first) with who/when/probe/statistics and whether each still matches the machine (validity: G31 trigger height, hash of the configuration, probe, age), and the compensation active now (type, file, taper height, mean and deviation).

accept_stale.desc: Load it although it no longer matches the machine (G31 Z or the configuration changed).

id.desc: Mesh id from machine.mesh.list: m-... of the library.

machine.mesh.load.desc: Loads a map of the library and activates it (the file is placed in sys/heightmap.csv and G29 S1 is sent). Refused with a job or a procedure running; refused when the map does not match the machine unless accept_stale is true.

machine.mesh.save.desc: Saves the map active now into the library (a copy made by the service; the firmware command G29 S3 is not used).

height.desc: Taper height in mm (M376 H): full compensation at Z=0, none from this height; 1 or less disables the taper.

machine.mesh.taper.desc: Sets the taper height of the compensation (M376 H).

machine.motion.get.desc: The motion parameters per axis and extruder from the object model and the M569 lines of the configuration: current (M906), idle factor and timeout, standstill and percent current (M913 / M917), microstepping and interpolation, speed, acceleration, jerk, backlash, driver mode and direction. What the board did not report is null and listed in `unavailable`.

machine.offsets.get.desc: The tool offsets (per tool, per axis, and which were probed) and the nine work offsets G54..G59.3 from the object model, the work system selected now and the last snapshot stored.

machine.offsets.snapshot.desc: Stores the tool and work offset tables in the calibration history (kind offsets.snapshot) and returns the differences with the previous snapshot. A snapshot is for comparing (it is not restored): the work offsets are the zones of the Workbench, the tool offsets persist through machine.config.plan kind config.g10.

machine.overview.desc: Summary of the calibration state for every role: per kind of calibration its traffic light (never / ok / old) and age in days, what the machine is ready for (homed, probe, mesh active, kinematics supported, levelling mode) and whether a procedure is running. No values of offsets or limits.

machine.power.get.desc: What the machine does when the supply drops: the M911 line of the configuration (cut voltage S, restore voltage R, commands P), whether resurrect.g (left by a job that was running) and resurrect-prologue.g exist, and the supply voltage now. Changing S and R is machine.config.plan config.m911 (administrator). It also says whether the interrupted job can be resumed (resume.checks) and what the person has to acknowledge (resume.needs_ack).

ack.desc: Laser / CNC: {piece, tool, area} all true (the part is where it was, the tool is the right one, the area is clear).

machine.power.resume.desc: Resumes the job left by a power cut (M916: the prologue runs first, in laser / CNC it asks again on the machine). The service checks again that the machine is idle, the supply is back, the job file is on the card and the prologue exists; it sends nothing otherwise.

full.desc: true: the status report of the whole machine.

id.desc: Record id: the report of one calibration.

machine.report.desc: The DATA of a printable report (the page draws it): one calibration (values, who, when, the mesh grid or the level residual) or the status of the whole machine (newest record of every kind, limits, offsets, active mesh and a fresh safety check).

kind.desc: Procedure: bedcal.preheat, bedcal.tune, homing.verify, level.g30, level.g32, level.measure, mesh.probe, offsets.verify, probe.read, probe.repeat, safety.check, shaping.tune. The others of the design answer not_implemented: probe.accuracy, probe.trigger, probe.offset, homing.repeat.

params.desc: Parameters of the procedure. probe.read: probe 0-15, samples 1-20, interval_s 0-5. probe.repeat: probe, samples 2-100, x and y (where the probe touches), deploy_each. level.g32 / level.g30 / level.measure: probe, passes, tolerance, points [{x, y}], verify, rehome_z. mesh.probe: probe, nx, ny, region {x0, x1, y0, y1}, margin, run_g32, name, save. homing.verify: axes (letters), tolerance 0.001-2 mm (needs confirm). safety.check: none. shaping.tune (needs an accelerometer, refused with no_accelerometer): axis, accelerometer, samples, travel, start, feed, cycles (needs confirm).

machine.run.desc: Starts a calibration procedure IN THE SERVICE: it reserves the movement (denied with a job, a live job, the bridge active or somebody else holding it), sends only the G-code of a closed list, publishes the progress (plugin data machine, or machine.runs) and stores the result and the audit record. Answers {run_id, kind, state} at once; one procedure at a time. The refusal reasons are in error.reason (no_probe, not_homed, unsupported_kinematics, heater_fault, busy_run).

run_id.desc: Only this run (to re-attach after the page was reloaded).

machine.runs.desc: The procedures started by machine.run: the one in progress (current) and the last finished ones, newest first, with state (queued, running, stopping, done, error, aborted), progress, result and error code.

machine.shaping.get.desc: The input shaper of the board (move.shaping: type, frequency, damping, amplitudes, delays; null for what it did not report), the types that can be set, the M593 lines of the configuration and the accelerometer capability (present, source, items).

size.desc: Side of the square in mm, 10-200 (50).

machine.shaping.test.desc: Generates the G-code of a ringing test (squares at several accelerations) as TEXT. It is never sent to the machine: save it and run it as a job. Refused when the square does not fit inside the limits of the axes.

machine.state.desc: Full state for the Machine page: the overview, the modules that are available (or hidden with the reason), the procedure runs, the newest calibration records with their values, the maintenance state and the machine block of the profile.

machine.stop.desc: Stops the procedure in progress (never refused, any role, no login): it ends at its next step, retracts the probe if it was deployed and releases the movement. It does NOT send M112 (the emergency stop stays the DWC / Jog function).

axis.desc: Axis letter to move (X Y Z U V W A B C).

distance.desc: Distance in mm, relative (0.1 to 200, negative goes back).

machine.test_move.desc: The test move of the steps-per-mm assistant: G91, G1 <axis><distance> F<feed> S0, G90 (the laser never fires). Level 3 confirmation; refused unless the machine is idle, the axis homed and the move inside its travel.

machine.tool.get.desc: The tools the machine has now (number, name, heaters, drives, fans, offsets), the next free tool number and the mode of the machine (Laser / CNC / FFF).

kind.desc: Optional capability to ask for: pwm, digital, adc, temp (temperature input), spi or servo.

machine.tool.pins.desc: The pins of the board no line of the configuration uses, with what each one can do, and the ones that are in use with the command that uses them.

spec.desc: The tool as in the design: type, number, name, heaters, fans, sensors, output, drive, offsets.

machine.tool.preview.desc: The exact configuration lines the plan config.tool would write for this tool, or what is wrong with it. Writes nothing.

action.desc: start (default), keep (the trial stays) or revert (put it back now).

gcode_kind.desc: What is tried: M208 limits, M92 steps/mm, M906 currents (and idle), M913, M917, M203 speeds, M201 accelerations, M205 / M566 jerk, M425 backlash, M556 skew, M593 input shaping. M376 answers not_implemented. M208, M92, M906, M913 and M917 need an administrator.

values.desc: Per kind, like the values of machine.config.plan of the same kind (M208: {axes: {"X": {min, max}}}).

machine.try.desc: Tries a VOLATILE value and puts the previous one back after `seconds` unless keep is sent, even if the page was closed or the service restarted. One trial at a time; denied with a job. M906 stays within the current cap of the profile. Making it permanent is machine.config.plan (keep answers with the kind and values to use).

machine.try.pending.desc: The volatile trial waiting for its automatic revert, if any (so a page that was reloaded can keep or revert it).

machine.workarea.get.desc: The work area of each mode (Laser, CNC, FFF; null = not measured) read from cutarea.g, the travel of X and Y, the mode in use, which of the corner macros are on the SD and whether X and Y are homed.

machine.workarea.positions.desc: The positions the jog saved ({name, x, y, z} in machine coordinates, where the tool was): two of them can be the opposite corners of a work area. Read only.

machine.workarea.release.desc: Releases the X and Y motors (macro handfree.g; Z stays firm) so the pointer can be taken to a corner by hand. The position is lost until the next homing. Level 4 confirmation.

rect.desc: {xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax} in bed coordinates (where the pointer lands): at least 10 mm each way, inside the travel of X and Y.

remove.desc: true with no rect: the mode goes back to not measured.

machine.workarea.save.desc: Saves the area of one mode (the others stay as they are), keeps a copy of the previous cutarea.g and loads it now when no job runs.

action.desc: capture: measure the corner at the end stops and answer {x, y}; goto: the pointer over X Y (laser off); frame: walk the saved area of the mode in use with the pointer.

machine.workarea.step.desc: One step of the corner assistants: reserves the movement (refused during a job) and runs the macro handcorner.g / gotobed.g / framecutarea.g (the pointer, never the laser: S0). Level 3 confirmation: the machine moves by itself.

meter.desc: Key of the meter to remove (empty: the main one).

meter.forget.desc: Removes a meter from the configuration (another one becomes the main one if needed); the saved readings are kept. Logged in Activity.

meter.desc: Key of a meter. Accepted, but the answer always lists every meter.

meter.get.desc: Returns the configured energy meters (Tuya) with their settings and the order in which the power off cuts them; local keys are masked.

id.desc: Tuya device id of the meter.

ip.desc: IP address of the meter on the local network, for example 192.168.1.50.

key.desc: Local key of the device as text (empty: keep the saved one when the id is the same).

meter.desc: Key of the meter to add or change (empty: the main one).

name.desc: Name shown for the meter (a new meter without a name uses its key).

version.desc: Tuya protocol version of the meter: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 or 3.5 (default 3.3).
