meter.save.desc: Tries the meter and, only if it answers, saves it (adds a meter or changes one, keeping its kWh history continuous). Logged in Activity.

meter.search.desc: Scans the local network for Tuya devices (about 8 seconds) and lists their IP, id and version, and which meter already uses each one.

changes.desc: Any of: nombre, inside_of (key of the meter it is part of, or null), feeds_pi (feeds the system: cut last), corta (cut by the power off), orden (cut order, lower first), vigila (null or {calentador, threshold_w, cortar}: alarm when it draws power with that heater off).

meter.desc: Key of the meter (empty: the main one, the one that feeds the system).

meter.settings.desc: Changes the settings of one meter: name, parent meter, whether it feeds the system, whether the power off cuts it, cut order and watched heater. Logged in Activity.

id.desc: Tuya device id of the meter.

ip.desc: IP address of the meter on the local network, for example 192.168.1.50.

key.desc: Local key of the device as text (empty: keep the saved one).

meter.desc: Key of the meter being edited (empty: the main one); its saved local key is used when key is empty and the id is the same.

version.desc: Tuya protocol version of the meter: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 or 3.5 (default 3.3).

meter.test.desc: Tries to read a Tuya meter with the given data (power, voltage, current, energy) without saving anything.

modules.list.desc: Lists the internal processes of the service with the way each one runs (auto / on / off), whether it runs now and why (a plugin that needs it is enabled, or forced).

mode.desc: auto: runs only while a plugin that needs it is enabled; on: always; off: never (applies at the next start of the service).

process.desc: Id of the internal process (as listed by modules.list).

modules.set.desc: Chooses how an internal process of the service runs. Saved in the configuration.

origin.desc: Who asks (page or program name); default: the origin of the call.

text.desc: Description of the action. Accepted but not used by the decision.

token.desc: Token of the caller's own reservation, so it does not count against it.

motion.ask.desc: Asks whether an origin may do a class of action now: allow, confirm or deny with the reason. Nothing is reserved; a confirmed call turns confirm into allow for 60 s.

motion.release.desc: Ends a reservation so the others can move again.

seconds.desc: New duration from now, 1 to 900 seconds (default 30).

motion.renew.desc: Extends a reservation that has not expired yet.

action.desc: Class of what will be done (default sequence).

origin.desc: Who reserves (shown to the others as the reason).

seconds.desc: Duration, 1 to 900 seconds (default 30); renew it before it expires.

text.desc: Short description shown to the others while it lasts.

motion.reserve.desc: Reserves the machine for a sequence: other origins are denied until it ends. Answers a token (motion.renew, motion.release) or the refusal.

motion.state.desc: Returns the state of the movement owner (what the machine is doing, reservations), the same as data.motion.

action.desc: Class of what will be done (default sequence).

origin.desc: Who takes the control (shown to the others).

seconds.desc: Duration, 1 to 900 seconds (default 30); renew it before it expires.

text.desc: Short description shown to the others while it lasts.

motion.take_over.desc: Takes the control of the movement from the device or person that has it (technician or administrator). The previous owner is stopped and warned (data.motion.notice) and the call goes to the audit. During a file job, a live job or bridge activity only an administrator may. Answers a token like motion.reserve.

axes.desc: Axes and extruders, for example ["X","E0"], or "all".

motors.disable.desc: Disables motors with M18: no holding torque and the homing is lost (a vertical axis can fall). Refused with a job or the machine busy; asks the movement owner; level 4 confirmation.

axes.desc: Axes and extruders, for example ["X","E0"], or "all".

motors.enable.desc: Enables motors with M17 (axes and extruders). Refused with a job running (file or live) or the machine busy. Logged in Activity.

motors.reread.desc: Asks the motors poller to read again which drivers are enabled (the result is published in the plugin data).

idle_s.desc: Seconds with the machine idle and no activity after which an open live job is closed by itself; 0 = not by this.

mode.desc: protected = a live job or the G-code bridge block the movement (jog, Workbench, Vision...); duet = like Duet / DWC: only a file job blocks.

release_s.desc: Seconds of quiet (no orders from the bridge, live job without activity) that free the movement in protected mode; default 20.

movement.lock.desc: Sets how the movement is locked for everything (jog, Workbench, Vision, frame...). Saved. Without arguments it only reports.

acknowledge_outbound.desc: Required true to turn them on: the events (and photos or videos if chosen) are sent to a third-party server, ntfy.sh unless another one is set.

on.desc: true sends notifications, false sends none (events are still logged).

notifications.active.desc: Turns every phone notification on or off. They are OFF by default because turning them on sends data out of the machine to a third-party server; turning them on is refused unless acknowledge_outbound is true. Saved and logged in Activity.

server.desc: ntfy server starting with http:// or https:// (empty: https://ntfy.sh).

topic.desc: ntfy topic: letters, numbers, - and _, up to 64 characters.

notifications.destination.desc: Changes the ntfy server and topic the notifications go to. Saved and logged in Activity.

notifications.get.desc: Returns the phone notification settings (ntfy destination, event types and options, quiet hours, mute) and the catalogue of event types.

minutes.desc: Minutes to mute, up to 1440; 0 unmutes now.

notifications.mute.desc: Mutes the phone notifications for N minutes (events are still logged), or unmutes them with 0. Logged in Activity.

notifications.new_topic.desc: Replaces the ntfy topic with a new random one; the phone has to subscribe again. Saved and logged in Activity.

attachment.desc: What is attached to the notification: none, a photo or a short video.

camera.desc: Camera of the photo or video of this type: a camera id, or "auto" / "" for the default camera of the notices.

default_camera.desc: Without type: the camera of the photo or video of every type that does not choose its own: a camera id, or "auto" for the main one.

priority.desc: ntfy priority; auto goes back to the default of the type.

quiet_hours.desc: Whether the quiet hours apply to this type.

type.desc: Event type id (catalogue in notifications.get). Without it only default_camera is changed.

notifications.option.desc: Changes the options of one event type (attachment, priority, quiet hours, camera); only the arguments given change. Without type, default_camera sets the camera the notices use unless their type chooses another. Whether a notice carries a photo or a video is decided here (the attachment of each type), not by the camera service. Saved.

mode.desc: mute: nothing is sent; soft: sent without sound.

notifications.quiet_hours.desc: Sets the daily quiet hours of the notifications; only the arguments given change. Saved and logged in Activity.

notifications.send.desc: Sends a phone notification now to the configured ntfy topic (for macros and jobs); it does not look at the type switches, quiet hours or mute.

type.desc: Event type id (catalogue in notifications.get): tests that type with its own attachment, priority and camera, skipping its switch, the quiet hours and the mute. Without it, a plain test.

notifications.test.desc: Sends a test notification to the configured destination and returns whether it was accepted, with the settings. With a type it sends what a real event of that type would send, marked as a test.

on.desc: true sends this type to the phone, false does not.

type.desc: Event type id, for example job_end, error, power, fuego (catalogue in notifications.get).

notifications.type.desc: Turns the phone notifications of one event type on or off. Saved.

notifications.video.desc: Sets the length of the short video attached to the notifications that use video. Saved.

categories.desc: Which kinds of file: config, zones, macros, system (default all).

replace.desc: Paths (as listed by package.preview) to replace although they differ; the old file is kept as <file>.bak-import.

package.apply.desc: Imports a package. It creates the files that are missing, never overwrites one (it keeps yours and reports the conflict) unless named in replace, and leaves the machine modes as references in sys/workshop/imported/.

categories.desc: Which kinds of file: config, zones, macros, system (default all).

package.export.desc: Builds the configuration package: the settings of the pages, the work zones, the macros of the person and the machine modes, in a zip (base64 in data). Secrets, users, keys and the database never go in.

categories.desc: Which kinds of file: config, zones, macros, system (default all).

package.preview.desc: Says what importing a package would do to each file (create, same, conflict, reference, skip) without writing anything.

password.clear.desc: Removes the DWC password: comments out M551 in sys/config.g (with a backup copy) and sets the default "reprap". Needs a confirmation.

password.desc: New password: 10 to 60 characters, not only letters or only digits, not a common one (or one with a 1, 123 or ! tail), not the name of a person, of the machine or its address, not a repetition or a sequence, and without " ' ; { } \ or control characters (they break the line M551 of config.g). Refused with 422 invalid_args and error.reason (characters, length, factory, mismatch, one_class, common, names, pattern). Never kept in the history.

repeat.desc: The password typed a second time: when given it must be equal (reason mismatch). Never kept in the history.

password.set.desc: Sets or changes the DWC password: writes M551 in sys/config.g (with a backup copy) and applies it at once. Logged in Activity; needs a confirmation.

password.status.desc: Says whether DWC has a password (an active M551 in sys/config.g), as {"set": true | false | null (config.g not readable)}; it is never shown.

file.desc: File name of the job it is armed for (job.file.fileName).

pelletlayers.arm.desc: ARMS a profile for ONE job file: from then on, while that job is printing, the service sends M568 P<tool> S<temperatures> when the layer changes, always inside the limits of the profile and of each heater. It never switches a heater on or off. A pause holds; cancel, end or a refusal of the board disarm it and leave the temperatures as they are. It is dropped after an hour if the job never starts.

pelletlayers.disarm.desc: Stops applying the profile now and leaves the temperatures as they are. Never blocked.

pelletlayers.get.desc: One profile: {name, profile: {tool, heaters, mode, axis, max_temp, max_step, max_spread, points: [{at, temps}]}, rev}.

pelletlayers.list.desc: The pellet temperature-by-layer profiles: {profiles: [{name, tool, heaters, mode, axis, points, first, last}], rev}.

pelletlayers.remove.desc: Deletes a profile (not while it is armed).

pelletlayers.set.desc: Validates and saves one profile (creates or replaces it). Saving never heats anything: a profile does nothing until it is armed for a job. Invalid fields answer invalid_args with one message per field. A profile that is armed cannot be changed.

pelletlayers.status.desc: The armed run: {armed, phase, profile, file, layer, applied, limited, changes, next, reason}. phase: off, waiting, waiting_heat, waiting_layer, running, holding, ended.

pid.cancel.desc: Cancels the zone tuning: the heaters of the tool are switched off and their previous temperatures put back. Never blocked.

zones.desc: Every heater of the tool with its target: [{h: heater number, t: temperature in C}, ...].

pid.start.desc: Tunes the PID of every heater zone of a tool, one at a time with the others at working temperature (M568, M303): HEATS the tool and opens an active risk. Refused with a job or a heater faulted; switched off on any problem.

pid.status.desc: Returns the progress of the PID tuning of the zones of a tool, zone by zone.

pid.trace.desc: The record of the last PID tuning (M303), taken by the service while the heater is tuned: {trace: {heater, target, started_at, ended_at, points: [[seconds, temperature, power 0..1 or null], ...]} or null, running}.

plugins.stopped.get.desc: Ids of the workshop plugins that a person stopped on purpose (the kiosk does not put them back in the enabled list). Returns {stopped: [ids]}.

id.desc: Id of the plugin; only the workshop plugins (they start with Workshop, for example WorkshopCamera).

stopped.desc: true records that the plugin was stopped on purpose; false forgets it (the plugin was started again).

plugins.stopped.set.desc: Records that a plugin was stopped on purpose (or started again) so kiosk/ensure-emergencyfab.sh does not reactivate it. An operator may. Returns {stopped: [ids], changed}; an id that is not a workshop plugin answers invalid_args.

armed.desc: true arms, false disarms, "toggle" switches the current state.

power.after_job.desc: Arms or disarms the power off at the end of the current job (or of the next one that starts); sys/daemon.g then runs the power off of power.off. Saved, mirrored in global.powerOffOnFinish and logged in Activity.

power.full_reset.desc: Restarts everything by software without cutting the power: asks the system to reboot and resets the board with M999. Whatever is running stops and homing is lost. Needs a confirmation.

method.desc: auto (the meter if one is configured, else the relay if set, else PS_ON if the board has it, else only the system), meter (the Tuya meter cuts the whole machine), relay (an output of the board cuts all the power), pson (M81 switches off the power supply controlled by PS_ON).

power_off_system.desc: With PS_ON, also shut the Raspberry Pi (the system) down; the meter and relay methods always shut it down.

relay_output.desc: Board output that drives the relay (the P number of its M950 line), 0 to 63.

relay_value.desc: Value written with M42 to that output to CUT the power: 0 or 1.

power.method.desc: Chooses how power.off, the timer and the power off after the job cut the power. Only the arguments given change; saved, logged in Activity; the answer says what will happen.

power.off.desc: Cuts the power of the whole machine with the chosen method (power.method): extra meters first, then sync, cut and system shutdown. Whatever is running stops. Needs a confirmation.

minutes.desc: Minutes from now until the power off, 1 to 720.

power.timer.desc: Schedules the power off of the whole machine in N minutes (the same power off as power.off; with a job running at that time it arms power.after_job instead). Saved, survives a restart of the service; logged in Activity.

power.timer_cancel.desc: Cancels the scheduled power off timer, if any (logged in Activity when there was one).

features.desc: Optional features to check as well: camera, vision (default: those enabled in DWC).

preflight.run.desc: Checks this installation (DSF and Python versions, SBC, folders, AppArmor, pip dependencies, power rules, ffmpeg/OpenCV, camera and Vision ports, DWC password, free space) and answers one item per check with ok, warn or error plus the fix in words.

process.desc: Id of the process (only the ones the list marks pausable: consumption, motors, maintenance, pid_trace, trace).

processes.pause.desc: Pauses a data process of the service: its loop keeps its heartbeat but does nothing until resumed. In memory only: a restart of the service runs it again.

process.desc: Id of the process (as for processes.pause).

processes.restart.desc: Asks a data process to end its loop and start again (the supervisor relaunches it at once, without an error or a wait). It is cooperative: a thread that is blocked inside a call cannot answer, so the call returns ok with requested=true and the process list shows restart_pending_s growing. Needs a confirmation in the page (level 2).

process.desc: Id of the process (as for processes.pause).

profile.get.desc: The declared machine profile (name, language, currency, meter, shutdown method, macro roles, probe, axis indexes, capability overrides, mode policies), the macro paths that really exist and the axis indexes found on the board.

changes.desc: Fields to change (the macros, axis_index, capability_overrides and mode_policies objects are merged by key; the others are replaced).

replace.desc: true takes changes as the whole profile instead of merging it into the current one.

profile.set.desc: Validates and saves the machine profile (sys/workshop/config/machine.json, atomic). Invalid fields answer invalid_args with one message per field.

readiness.list.desc: What each plugin's start-up card last reported: {plugins: {Id: {pending, total, skipped?, at}}}. A plugin that never reported is missing.

omitted.desc: The ids the page had put away when it reported (list of strings).

pending.desc: Rows still to configure (orange or red), never an optional one that is off.

plugin.desc: Id of the plugin whose start-up card reports (Workshop...).

rows.desc: The rows as the machine says them, before any decision: [{id, state: configured|example|missing|session|na, optional}]. With them the service recounts every time it is asked, applying the decisions of the settings file startup.

skipped.desc: Optional rows that are off or that the person chose not to use (not steps to do). Omitted = 0.

total.desc: Rows that are steps of the person (optional ones that are off or not in use are not counted).

readiness.report.desc: A plugin's start-up card tells the service how many rows are pending, so the service page can list them all. Nothing is written when the numbers did not change.

id.desc: Identifier given to risk.start.

risk.list.desc: Lists the active risks (level 4: the machine is without a protection), explicit and detected.

id.desc: Identifier of the risk, used to close it.

seconds.desc: Expires by itself after this many seconds (default 600; the service keeps it between 5 s and 6 h).

text.desc: Text of the warning in Spanish, or the only text the caller has (default: the id).

text_en.desc: Text of the warning in English; the pages show the one of the DWC language (default: text).

risk.start.desc: Opens or renews an active risk: the bar and the pages show a fixed warning and the strip paints the risk state until risk.end or the timeout.

camera.desc: Assume the camera is (or is not) allowed to a viewer.

mode.desc: Mode the machine is in now (laser, cnc, fff), if known.

modes.desc: Modes of an operator to assume (laser, cnc, fff).

prefix.desc: Only operations starting with this text.

role.desc: Or a role (base or custom); then modes default to all, camera to off.

user.desc: A person (their role, modes and camera are used).

roles.effective.desc: What a person or a role may do, operation by operation, with the reason of every block (role, denied, mode, camera) and whether it comes from the base role, a grant or a denial. `escalated` tells the same call when it changes settings or writes hardware parameters.

name.desc: A base role (viewer, operator, technician, admin) or a custom role.

roles.get.desc: One role: its definition, the people who have it and the operations it adds to or takes away from its base role.

roles.list.desc: Lists the custom roles (with how many people have each), the capabilities a grant or a denial may name, the operations that cannot be delegated and the limits.

roles.remove.desc: Deletes a custom role. Refused while somebody has it. Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps the role.

base.desc: Base role it starts from: viewer, operator or technician (never admin).

deny.desc: What it may NOT do even if its base role may (same kinds of entries). Stopping can never be denied. A denial wins over a grant.

grant.desc: What it may do on top of its base role: capability ids (see roles.list), operation names or patterns such as lights.*. Operations that cannot be delegated (users, roles, keys, passwords...) are refused. machine.hardware_params is the explicit key to the hardware-risk parameters (M208, M92, M906, M913, M917, M569, M584, prologue).

name.desc: Name of the custom role (1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots or hyphens; not the name of a base role).

roles.set.desc: Creates a custom role or replaces the one with that name (the whole definition is replaced). The change applies to the people who have it on their next call. Needs a confirmation; the audit keeps the role before and after.

safety.status.desc: Live state of the laser interlocks the machine profile declares (lid, extraction, key), read from the Duet inputs: {declared, ok, interlocks: [{name, capability, label, gpin, active_when, state}]}, state being ok, open or unknown (unknown counts as not ok). Without declared interlocks: declared false, ok true, empty list. In Laser mode a declared interlock that is not ok makes job.start and frame.start with the laser fail with interlock_open.

service.restart.desc: Restarts the whole service (the process ends with a non-zero code and DSF starts it again). The protections are off for a few seconds, so it is refused unless the machine is idle or off with no job, laser, movement or protection alarm: the refusal (code conflict) lists the reasons in error.reasons. It answers first and ends the process about a second later. Level 3 confirmation.

name.desc: Settings file: one of bed-estimates, bed-zones, bridge, buttons, camera, cameras, clamps, current, file-review, focus, gcodelib, jog, jog-macros, laser, laser-designs, layer-recipes, machine-calibrations, machine-maintenance, machine-pointsets, materials, motors, pellet-layers, printing, rs485, startup, step-ceiling, vision, work_state, zcal, zone-extra, zone-sizes, zone-zpoints (a name, never a path).

settings.get.desc: Reads a shared settings file and its revision: {value, rev}. value is null and rev "0" when the file does not exist yet.

name.desc: Settings file: one of bed-estimates, bed-zones, bridge, buttons, camera, cameras, clamps, current, file-review, focus, gcodelib, jog, jog-macros, laser, laser-designs, layer-recipes, machine-calibrations, machine-maintenance, machine-pointsets, materials, motors, pellet-layers, printing, rs485, startup, step-ceiling, vision, work_state, zcal, zone-extra, zone-sizes, zone-zpoints (a name, never a path).

patch.desc: Object whose top-level keys replace those of the file.

settings.merge.desc: Sets only some top-level keys of a shared settings file, with no revision check (for fields that do not clash with the work of others). Returns {value, rev, changed}. Noted in Activity.

base_rev.desc: The rev returned by settings.get ("0" for a file that does not exist yet).

name.desc: Settings file: one of bed-estimates, bed-zones, bridge, buttons, camera, cameras, clamps, current, file-review, focus, gcodelib, jog, jog-macros, laser, laser-designs, layer-recipes, machine-calibrations, machine-maintenance, machine-pointsets, materials, motors, pellet-layers, printing, rs485, startup, step-ceiling, vision, work_state, zcal, zone-extra, zone-sizes, zone-zpoints (a name, never a path).

value.desc: The whole new content (object or list).

settings.set.desc: Writes a shared settings file only if nobody changed it since base_rev was read; otherwise it answers the error 'conflict' with error.current = {value, rev} so the caller can merge and retry. Returns {rev, changed}. Noted in Activity.

pattern.desc: ok (one beep, default), done (three rising beeps), error (two low beeps) or attention (three short beeps).

sound.beep.desc: Plays a beep pattern with M300 (DWC sounds it on the screens where it is open); it answers at once and plays in the background.

apply.desc: Must be true: the explicit request.

items.desc: The items the person ticked: [{id, expected_sha, confirm_safety}]. Only these are applied, one by one.

machine_off.desc: The person states the machine is off (needed for safety files).

startup.apply.desc: Applies ONLY the items of startup.plan that the person ticked, each with the expected_sha of the preview (a file that changed since is skipped). Refused unless the board is idle. Safety files (pause, cancel, homing, laser guard, start-up) also need confirm_safety on the item and machine_off. The old file is first copied to sys/workshop/legacy/<date>/, writes are atomic and read back, and the run goes to the install log.

expected_sha.desc: The sha the person was looking at (the `sha` of startup.files): a file that changed since is refused.

path.desc: Path of the file relative to 0:/, as the list of files shows it.

reviewed.desc: true: leave the file as it is (the person edited it on purpose); false: ask for attention again.

startup.file.review.desc: Remembers that a hand-edited file was looked at and is meant to stay as it is. It is kept against the sha of the content: the file asks for attention again only when it changes again. Nothing on the SD is written; it only stores the decision in the service settings.

path.desc: Path of the file relative to 0:/, as the list of files shows it.

startup.file.view.desc: One file of the SD to read: is it there, its text (cut at 200 KB; network and password lines masked), what differs from the factory copy (line ranges and a flag per line) when there is one, and whether it was applied (the install log and the plan). Only files the plugins bring or the list shows; never users, keys or tokens. READ ONLY.

startup.files.desc: The files every workshop plugin brings (workshop-owned, templates, native files with workshop lines, generated and expected-external), each with its class, its state on the SD (ok, edited, missing, not yet generated, needs a look), who uses it and whether it is a safety file, plus counts per plugin. READ ONLY: it only reads the SD.

details.desc: false: only the summary (counts per state and kind), no file list.

only_problems.desc: true: in the file list keep only the files that need a person to look (edited, deleted, wrong mark, unknown extra).

startup.integrity.desc: Integrity report of the SD against the manifest of the workshop files (workshop-owned, templates, native files with workshop lines, generated files and files the person has to provide). READ ONLY: it never writes, restores or deletes anything.

apply.desc: Must be true: the explicit request.

expected_sha.desc: expected_sha of the preview (the sha of the current file, or 'absent'): a file that changed since is not replaced.

path.desc: Path of the file relative to 0:/.

startup.integrity.restore.desc: Restores ONE workshop-owned file from the factory copy, on explicit request only. Refused for templates, native, generated and external files, for anything that runs in pause, cancel, homing, the laser guard or at start-up, and unless the board is idle with no job, laser or movement. The current file is first copied to sys/workshop/legacy/<date>/, the write is atomic and the action goes to the install log.

path.desc: Path of the file relative to 0:/ (as listed by startup.integrity).

startup.integrity.restore.preview.desc: What restoring ONE workshop-owned file from the factory copy would do: refusals with their reason, the diff current -> factory and the expected_sha to send back. WRITES NOTHING.

startup.plan.desc: The start-up plan of THIS SD: the link blocks of the native files, the move of the mode files with the references that change, and the templates a new install is missing. Every item that changes a file carries its unified diff (secrets masked) and the expected_sha to send back. WRITES NOTHING.

startup.runs.get.desc: One run of the start-up with the action on every file: created, skipped (and why), failed, with the sha before and after. The text of a diff is included only for an administrator.

plugin.desc: Only the runs that touched a file of this plugin.

startup.runs.list.desc: The runs of the start-up (who, when, which plugins, counts per outcome), newest first.

keys.desc: Names of the data keys to return (for example motion, liveJob); empty returns every key.

state.get.desc: Returns the data the service publishes in the object model (plugins.WorkshopService.data) from its memory; nothing is asked to the board.

on.desc: true: automatic control by mode and state; false: switched off by hand.

statuslight.set.desc: Status LEDs of the strip: back to automatic control (on) or switched off by hand (off), with the macros light/statusledon.g / statusledoff.g.

cursor.desc: The cursor of the previous answer; empty = from the first sample.

job.desc: Id of the job (YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS, the id of the history) or "current" (default): the job being recorded, else the last one recorded (nothing once trace.json was deleted).

limit.desc: Most samples in one answer (default 2000, at most 10000); more = true when there are more right now.

trace.since.desc: Only the samples of a job's trace added since the cursor (file jobs and live jobs): {job, active, samples, cursor, done, more, reset, meta}. reset = true: the cursor was of another job or the samples were reduced, so they come from the first one and the client drops what it had. done = true: the job ended and every sample was sent. Asking for the job being recorded keeps the recorder awake (like view.heartbeat trace). Deleting trace.json forgets the last closed job: "current" answers nothing recorded until another job starts (its history copy is still read by its id). Unknown job: not_found.

modes.desc: Modes an operator may run: a list of laser, cnc, fff (default: only laser). Technicians and administrators have all.

name.desc: Name of the person (1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots or hyphens).

pin.desc: New PIN: 6 to 12 digits, not a run (345678), a repetition (454545), a probable date or a common PIN; PINs already saved keep working.

role.desc: viewer, operator, technician or admin, or the name of a custom role (roles.list).

users.add.desc: Adds a person. The first one created turns the identity on and has to be an administrator.

users.close_sessions.desc: Ends the session of every person except the administrator who asks (sessions now survive a restart of the service, so this is how everybody is made to sign in again). Answers how many sessions ended.

enabled.desc: False switches the roles off: nobody is asked to identify and everybody is an administrator again, the people stay saved. True switches them on.

pin.desc: The PIN of the administrator who asks (needed to switch off).

users.enable.desc: Switches the roles and PINs on or off without deleting the people. Switching off ends every session and needs the administrator's PIN; it also opens the camera and Vision on the network.

users.list.desc: Lists the people with their role, modes and last activity, and the session settings.

users.remove.desc: Removes a person and ends their sessions. Not yourself, not the last administrator.

pin.desc: New PIN: 6 to 12 digits, not a run (345678), a repetition (454545), a probable date or a common PIN; PINs already saved keep working.

users.reset_pin.desc: Sets a new PIN for a person and ends their sessions.

modes.desc: Modes an operator may run: a list of laser, cnc, fff (default: only laser). Technicians and administrators have all.

role.desc: viewer, operator, technician or admin, or the name of a custom role (roles.list).

users.set.desc: Changes role, modes or camera of a person. Nobody changes their own role and the last administrator stays.

anonymous_viewer.desc: A caller with no login may read the state as a viewer (touch screen).

idle_minutes.desc: Minutes without activity before a session expires.

max_hours.desc: Longest life of a session, active or not.

never_expires.desc: Sessions never expire (the two limits above are ignored); they end by logging out or by `users.close_sessions`.

users.settings.desc: Reads or changes the session settings (without arguments it only reads).

topic.desc: health (System health and Services pages), power (Consumption page), motors (Motors page), trace (job trace view) or lights_board (Lights page, Advanced tab).

view.heartbeat.desc: Tells the service a page is visible (send every ~10 s): the pollers of that topic work at full speed; without heartbeats they sleep after ~30 s.

vision.get.desc: Reads a JSON answer of the Vision service (state, camera orientation, head position, lens calibration). Fails with a clear message if Vision is off.

body.desc: JSON body of the request (the arguments of that Vision path). Empty: no arguments.

path.desc: Vision path to call: /photo, /detect, /record/search, /measure (only where Vision announces the measure capability, see docs/MACHINE-PHASE4-CONTRACT.md). Vision's own settings are not changed here: they go through settings.set (name vision).

vision.post.desc: Calls the Vision service: takes a photo, detects shapes or searches the record. A detection may take several seconds.

workstate.get.desc: Reads the work state shared by every screen: per zone the Prepare steps done and the focus applied, and the focus height. Returns {state, rev}; state is empty when nothing was saved yet.

state.desc: Part of the work state to record: {v: 1, zones: {"<zone>": {prepare: {measure: ts, border: ts}, applied: {z, ts}}}, focus_h: {h, base, ts}}. ts is epoch milliseconds (negative for a cleared mark). Unknown keys or wrong values refuse the whole call.

workstate.set.desc: Records the work state (an operator may). It is merged into what is stored mark by mark and the newest time wins, so what did not change is not overwritten. Returns {state, rev, changed} with the merged state. Noted in the audit like any write.
